judge: second judge, run 2 stage 7 round 2, blind to audit_r2data_round2_judgments.json
source: data/work/audit_r2data_round2_judge_input.json (quotes and label definitions only); the task named audit_r2data_judge_input.json, which is the round 1 input and differs in 4 cells
criterion: supported when the quoted text states the value under the label definition (auditor.md check b: value present in the quote)

judgments.reason: Quote 1 names AI/ML clusters as a target of large-scale photonic switches, which is direct fit, so yes.

judgments.value: Flip-chip bond to a ceramic interposer with a land grid array; wire-bonded ceramic package with a 68-fiber ribbon attached; feedback controlled stabilization without a chip cooling system; air trenches cut chip power
judgments.reason: All four parts are stated: flip-chip to ceramic interposer with LGA, wire-bonded ceramic package with 68-fiber ribbon, feedback stabilization with no chip cooling, power cut by air trenches.
Reports development of a switch device, a lab-level prototype; nothing suggests pilot or production.
Quote 1 places the technology at proof-of-concept in lab before commercialization; quote 2 is a fabricated device, both lab.
Quote 1 is a three-waveguide switch for photonic integrated circuits and quote 2 says the fabrics are on a single chip, so light stays in on-chip waveguides.
Quote 1 is a product launch of the G5 Robotic Patch Panel, i.e. sold as a product, which the definition counts as production (vendor claim).

judgments.value: Crossing loss grows with port count; control units and drive wiring grow quickly with port count; high heater power
judgments.reason: Crossing loss growing with ports and control units/wiring growing with ports are stated as limits; high power from the thermo-optic effect is stated as a drawback though not tied to port count (weakest part).

judgments.value: Multicore-fiber collimator, spatial multiplexer array and LCoS spatial light modulator integrated in one prototype
judgments.reason: Quote states the prototype integrates an MCF collimator, spatial mux/demux array and LCoS SLM, which is exactly the value.
Switches fabricated for the first time is a fabricated device, lab.
A fiber-handling robot physically reconnects optical connectors, which is mechanical_fiber.
Apollo is described as a large-scale production deployment that forms most of the data center networks, production.

judgments.value: Aluminum nitride interposer and 64-channel lidless fiber array; through glass via interposer and pitch reducing fibre array; pluggable package; CMOS driver chiplets; unpackaged switch reliable over 10 billion cycles
judgments.reason: Each of the five parts is stated: AlN interposer with 64-channel lidless fiber array, TGV interposer with pitch reducing fibre array, pluggable package, CMOS driver chiplets, 10 billion cycles without packaging.
An implemented prototype, lab.
MCF collimator array plus MEMS mirror array matches the free_space_bulk definition (collimators and mirrors).
Quote 2 says the OCS platform is designed specifically for AI data center networking, direct fit, so yes.
Reflective 2D MEMS means mirrors steering beams, which the definition places in free_space_bulk; inferred from 'reflective', free space is not named outright.
Demonstrated 16x16 switches fabricated by surface micro-machining, lab.
Only application named is fiber optic telecommunications, which the definition maps to none, so no.
Integrated OCS combining silicon photonics with MEMS actuation, light in on-chip waveguides.
Quote says free-space-optics-based switch outright.
Proposes a reconfigurable optical DCN; reconfigurable topologies count as yes in the comparison-framework question (under the ocs-domain analog alone it would read as indirect).
Piezo actuators align collimated beams between opposing fiber arrays, free_space_bulk.
Reconfigurable network across racks and nodes, and beam-steering switches as central cluster and intercluster switches, is a reconfigurable topology for clusters, yes.
Silicon wire waveguides and an optical switch chip with MZI elements and waveguide crossings, integrated_photonic.
Says the demonstrations still need advances to move from research to product, so lab.
Co-integration with GPUs and collapsing the multi-tier network to one tier (spine replacement) are direct fit, yes.
Data center scale interconnect and HPC routing are general data center use, indirect, so partial.
SOAs as on-chip gain and switch elements on InP, integrated_photonic.
Designed, fabricated and demonstrated monolithic 4x4 cross-connect, lab.
OCS replacing the electrical switches in the core of the network is spine replacement, direct, so yes; the quote is generic OCS motivation and does not name SOA or AI (weakest yes).
Only intelligent buildings and optical access networks are named, none, so no.
